thread:
maria_pm: Quick design check — I pushed a new Figma frame for the routing policies editor microflows. Key asks: make priority ordering clearer, improve validation copy (users keep misreading the tie-breaker behavior), and check keyboard drag/drop a11y.
aj_design: Taking a look now. Two quick notes from the mock: the current chevron + drag handle feels visually noisy. Can we try a subtle hover-only drag affordance and a persistent small 'priority' badge instead?
devon_frontend: Hover-only drag makes sense performance-wise. Curious how that interacts with touch though — need an always-visible handle for mobile. Also, if we switch to hover-only, we should ensure focus styles reveal the handle for keyboard users.
samir_research: From the usability study (n=12) we saw users confused by "higher priority first" wording. They expect '1' to be top, but some thought higher number==higher priority. Suggest copy: "Lower number = higher priority (1 runs before 2)" and show a tiny inline example: 1 -> matches first.
maria_pm: Good point. Aj, can you propose two copy variants? One concise and one explanatory for first-time users.
aj_design: Concise: "Priority: lower numbers run first." Explanatory: "Priority (numeric): lower numbers run before higher numbers. Example: 1 will be evaluated before 2." I'll add the inline example under the header with subtle gray text.
devon_frontend: For validation states: current red toast "Rule conflict" is too vague. We should inline the issue on the rule row and add a tooltip that explains how to resolve (e.g., reorder, change condition). Inline text: "Conflict with rule X — both match the same input; adjust priority or conditions." That way the toast can be a soft alert rather than blocking.
aj_design: Agree. Also add an inline 'preview' badge that opens the simulation sandbox anchored to that row. PM asked for quick-run preview per-rule.
maria_pm: Yes — product wants per-rule preview. It should run the example prompt and show which route would match. Keep it ephemeral and non-blocking.
samir_research: Accessibility: keyboard users need clear focus for rows and accessible labels for drag/drop. Suggest aria-grabbed and live region updates during reordering so screen readers announce "Rule moved to position 2". We should also provide a keyboard-only reorder control (move up/move down buttons) visible in condensed mode.
aj_design: I'll add both: a small move up/down chevron pair (visually hidden in mouse mode, shown on focus or when condensed) and the drag handle that appears on hover/focus. Also update the color contrast on the priority badge — current gray fails AA at small size.
devon_frontend: Implementation note: we already have a performant virtualized list component used in other consoles. We can reuse it, but we must preserve per-row KV cache for previews. For the live preview, let's throttle calls (500ms debounce) and show a spinner in the preview panel.
ci-bot: Deploy preview build available at https://deploy-previews.redwood.sh/1849-routing-ux — includes initial hover affordance and priority badge color adjustments. :rocket:
maria_pm: Thanks CI. Aj — can you drop the updated Figma link and the two copy variants into this thread? Also include the exact aria strings you want.
aj_design: Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/Routing-Editor-1849
Copy variants pasted below:
- Concise: "Priority: lower numbers run first. Use integers (1, 2, 3)."
- Explanatory: "Priority (numeric): Rules with lower numbers are evaluated before rules with higher numbers. Example: 1 runs before 2. If two rules are equal priority, the editor uses left-to-right order as a tiebreaker."
Aria strings:
- row container: role="listitem" aria-label="Routing rule: <rule name>" aria-posinset="<position>" aria-setsize="<total>"
- drag handle: role="button" aria-label="Reorder rule" aria-grabbed="false"
- live region: role="status" aria-live="polite" "
devon_frontend: I'll wire those aria attributes. For the tiebreaker text in the explanatory copy — let's soften: "If two rules have the same priority, the editor falls back to left-to-right order (top to bottom)." keeps it plain.
samir_research: One more microinteraction: when a rule is invalid/has conflict, add an exclamation icon with tooltip text and `aria-describedby` pointing to an offscreen description for screen readers.
maria_pm: This all sounds good. Next steps: Aj update Figma and drop final assets + copy, Devon build keyboard reorder + inline validation UI, Samir add the a11y spec doc snippet, I'll sync with Product on rollout and canary gating.
aj_design: Uploaded updated frames and a short prototype (drag + keyboard). Figma note: I added a 'preview' flyout anchored to the right of each row and a 'run example' shortcut (Ctrl+Enter) in the sandbox.
ci-bot: E2E tests for keyboard reorder added in PR #4523.
maria_pm: Targeting canary for next Wednesday. If anyone sees major regressions in the preview deploy link, flag here. Thanks everyone! :heart:
